text: One decision has been outstanding since Lesson 1: when systems disagree, which one wins. This lesson makes it official.

Three domains resolve in one meeting: Atlas wins for Product and Order, because it's the only system that does that job. Beacon wins for marketing consent, because it's the only system that actually captures it.

Customer identity doesn't resolve that easily. The owners agree to build a golden record in Summit instead: matched on Email across all three systems, order history always from Atlas, contact details from whichever source was most recently updated, and marketing consent always from Beacon.

This is the exact mechanism that would have answered the Lesson 1 access request in minutes instead of six weeks — one golden Customer ID, with every field traceable to the rule that produced it. And the decision itself gets logged, not just agreed to verbally, so it survives the next reorg.
Next: Lesson 10 designs access and retention policies for this same golden record and the CDEs behind it.
